Subj:   Ledge Street Elementary Playground 
 
Aldermanic Resolution R-26-048 authorized $247,386.18 to construct a new Ledge Street 
Elementary playground.  The existing playground, which is actually sited on City Park & 
Recreation land, is quite old with many of its components approaching end of useful life.  This 
project will create a new playground in the old ballfield behind the school.   
 
The school proposes to utilize O’Brien & Sons to purchase the playground equipment.  We will 
be taking advantage of the Massachusetts Higher Education Consortium (MHEC), which 
provides pre-bid, publicly compliant cooperative contracts for higher education, K-12, 
municipalities, libraries, and non-profit organizations across New England.  O’Brien & Sons is 
one of the successful bidders under this arrangement, and the Nashua School District is a 
member of MHEC.   We have used a similar consortium called Sourcewell for past purchases 
including vehicles and the last turf installation at Stellos Stadium. 
 
The actual playground equipment being purchased and the layout will be presented by Michelle 
Mills, 2nd grade teacher at Ledge Street, who has spearheaded the effort to obtain the 
necessary funds as well as working with O’Brien & Sons to select grade appropriate structures 
for the students at Ledge Street Elementary.   The Nashua School District has a large inventory 
of the “Landscape Structures” product provided by O’Brien & Sons and we have standardized 
our maintenance plan around them. 
 
Plant Operations will be responsible for the actual playground installation, including ground 
preparation for the rubberized surface.  We will also provide appropriate security cameras to 
view the complete playground. 
 
Recommendation to approval a contract with M.E. O’Brien & Sons, Inc. of Medway, 
Massachusetts, to provide the Ledge Street Elementary playground equipment and rubber 
surfacing in the amount of $247,147.20.  Funding is from account 91.1001.994600-081100-
0000 account (City Hall).

THIS AGREEMENT is made and entered into on the date last written below, by and between Nashua School District, 
SAU 42 (hereinafter "Employer"), and Beacon Communication Services LLC, an independent contractor (hereinafter 
"Contractor"). 
WHEREAS, the Employer desires to retain the services of Contractor, and Contractor desires to render services to the 
Employer, upon the terms and conditions hereinafter stated: 
NOW, THEREFORE, the parties hereto, intending to be legally bound hereby, do hereby promise and agree as follows: 
SECTION 1 – SCOPE OF DUTIES TO BE PROVIDED 
1.1 Term 
Employer agrees to hire Contractor for the remainder of the 2026/2027 school year, commencing September 29, 2026 
following execution of this Agreement and any required District approvals, and continuing through the end of the 
2026/2027 school year unless terminated in accordance with Section 4 of this Agreement. 
1.2 Duties 
Contractor agrees to perform work for the Employer on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement and agrees 
to devote the necessary time and attention, reasonable periods of illness and approved schedule changes excepted, to  
the performance of the duties specified herein. Contractor's duties may include the following:  
• Direct, in-person speech and language therapy 
• Speech and language evaluations and assessments 
• Attendance at referral, IEP, eligibility, progress, and other student -related meetings. The SLP may attend meetings in 
person or virtually/remotely depending on provider schedule, availability, and the needs of the assignment.  
• IEP development and related documentation 
• Progress report development 
• Evaluation summary reports and report writing 
• Direct and indirect service provision, including preparation/planning, IEP review, progress review, and outside 
evaluation review 
• Classroom, teacher, case manager, and other staff consultation  
• Observations and other general SLP/SLPA duties 
• Billing and attendance documentation 
• Data collection 
• Scheduling, case management, compliance activities, and other speech- language duties necessary to meet student 
and District needs 
• SLPA supervision provided by the SLP in accordance with applicable requirements. Supervision may be provided in 
person or remotely/virtually when permitted by applicable requirements and appropriate based on the SLP's 
schedule and the needs of the assignment. 
Caseload caps may be imposed when necessary to maintain appropriate service delivery, supervision, professional 
standards, and compliance. Caseload expectations and assignments may be reviewed collaboratively with District 
leadership based upon student needs, treatment units, service frequency , and provider capacity. 
Beacon Communication Services will generally aim to abide by the school district calendar and schedule. Contractor

Individual provider schedules and availability will be communicated at the onset of the contracted term, and 
reasonable efforts will be made to maintain those schedules throughout the term. This includes start time, end time, 
days worked, and scheduled time off. 
Contractor further agrees that in all aspects of such work, Contractor shall comply with applicable policies, standards, 
and regulations of the Employer communicated to Contractor and shall perform the contracted duties faithfully and 
professionally.

Tutoring Agreement for Students in the Nashua School District

Reach The Top Tutoring (herein referred to as RTTT) will provide tutoring services on the 
following basis: 
 
SERVICES: 
 
• Services will be for students who are determined by the district to be eligible for tutoring services. 
 
• Tutors will offer educational assistance at a mutually agreed upon location, and will assist the students 
in whatever academic areas are called for or required and approved. (This contract will cover remote 
services) 
 
• Each tutor assigned by RTTT will have a current criminal history background check on file. 
 
• All management and coordination tasks of tutors and clients will be handled by RTTT once the client 
has been referred to RTTT. 
 
• Clients will receive services for as many hours each week as are deemed necessary/desirable by a 
combination of input from involved parties, and approved by the Nashua School District.  
 
• Tutoring services will continue for each client for as long as the client is in need of them and they are 
deemed eligible and approved by the district. 
 
PROCESS: 
 
Set-up of each client referred to RTTT through this agreement will follow the same process steps from referral 
to the first tutoring hour.  The steps are outlined below: 
 
• RTTT office is called or emailed with contact and background information regarding a student in need 
of services.   
 
• Based on contact information, the student (parent/guardian) will be contacted by the RTTT owner and 
information regarding their situation, academic needs, personality (likes/dislikes/preferences for 
tutoring), and schedule will be collected. 
 
• Using the above information, a tutor will be assigned to the client from the pool of RTTT tutors. 
 
• The tutor will contact the client and set-up a first tutoring session. 
 
• Session cancellations or schedule changes will be handled by RTTT (see cancellation policy details in 
the terms section). 
 
• Each week tutors will report their contract hours to RTTT with signed RTTT report forms. 
 
• Reports detailing tutoring activities of each client will be sent upon request. 
 
TERMS OF SERVICE:
The following terms apply to each client receiving service as part of this agreement. 
 
Chaperone:  If tutoring takes place at the home at no time will a RTTT tutor act as a guardian for the client.  
Unless the client is an adult, a parent or guardian (at least 18 years of age) must be present during the entire 
tutoring session. 
 
Session Cancellation:  RTTT and/or the tutor must be given at least 2 hour notice if a scheduled session cannot 
be made.  Payment for the missed session will be required if proper notice is not given.   
 
Tardiness:  A tutor will wait at the tutoring location for the parent/guardian and student to arrive for 15 
minutes.  If the parent/guardian and student do not arrive within 15 minutes, the tutor will leave and payment 
will be expected for the missed session.  If the parent/guardian and student arrive before the tutor leaves, 
tutoring will be performed for the remainder of the scheduled session. 
 
Safety:  RTTT reserves the right to refuse to tutor a client if it is determined that a safe and appropriate learning 
environment does not exist at the desired tutoring location. 
 
Payment:  RTTT will submit invoices regularly.  Tutoring hours are submitted in 1/2 hour increments.  
Payment for submitted invoices will be expected on a 30 day net term.   
 
PRICING 
 
• RTTT will charge Nashua School District $80 per hour for time of scheduled tutor/client contact time.  
This contract will cover up to 10 hours per week of tutoring time. 
 
• RTTT will be billed for any time incurred by tutor i.e. meetings/discussions with district regarding 
student or prep time incurred in order to support student.  
 
• There will be no charge for mileage costs or driving time incurred by the tutor unless agreed upon and 
provided by both parties prior to the start of services.
